summary: Cattaraugus County, NY tower in Allegany State Park, built in 1928; still standing, but sources call for restoration and no recent condition report was found.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor LS40 steel fire lookout tower
facts.status_note: Still standing; Wikipedia says it needs adoption and restoration. No newer condition report found.

events.note: Built by the Conservation Department's Division of State Parks
Jurisdiction moved to Forest Fire Control for many park towers; Allegany State Park kept this one and staffed it in high fire danger

evidence.supports: in Allegany State Park, Coldspring, Cattaraugus County
evidence.quote: It is in Allegany State Park in Coldspring , Cattaraugus County
The Mt. Tuscarora Fire Tower still stands today, near Quaker Lake.

evidence.supports: built 1928 as a 60-foot steel fire lookout
evidence.quote: In 1928, a 60-foot-tall (18 m) steel fire lookout tower was built on the mountain.

evidence.supports: Division of State Parks built Aermotor LS40 tower
evidence.quote: Division of State Parks built a 60-foot-tall (18 m) Aermotor LS40 steel fire lookout tower on the mountain

evidence.supports: marker caption: 1928 tower on Mt. Tuscarora
evidence.quote: In 1928, a tower was constructed on Mt. Tuscarora and another in the Rice Brook area.

evidence.supports: 1931 transfer of many state park towers to Forest Fire Control
evidence.quote: In 1931, the jurisdiction of many State Park towers was transferred to Forest Fire Control.

evidence.supports: park kept jurisdiction and staffed the tower in high fire danger
evidence.quote: However, the Alleghany State Park retained jurisdiction and staffed the tower on Mount Tuscarora during times of high fire danger.
The lookout tower remains on the mountain, but is in serious need of adoption and restoration.

evidence.supports: Mount Irvine was the only park tower taken down in early 1970s
evidence.quote: When all the fire towers were abandoned in favor of aerial surveillance in 1971, the Mt. Irvine tower was the only one taken down by park personnel in the early 1970s.

evidence.supports: index lists Mount Tuscarora as a standing tower

notes_for_editor: Current condition and public access are unconfirmed. Wikipedia is the main source and cites no update after its restoration call. The marker page is about the Summit tower restoration; only its 1928 caption is cited. An online hiker post (Hike WNY group) says the stairs were removed and the tower is closed off, but we could not read it, so it is not used. Wikipedia gives 2,142 ft in the infobox and 2,144 ft in the text; elevation is not used. Wikipedia spells the park name Alleghany once; the park itself uses Allegany.
